# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-14 (Extended v117)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Summer Year 4, afternoon transitioning to evening)**: Paris—Café Musain near Panthéon; le Petit-Picpus convent district; M. Gillenormand's residences; Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Luxembourg gardens (Rue de l'Ouest side); village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; English provincial towns (Dunstead, Kelmere, Torton, Ostcombe, Ravenmere, Kelford, Yarlby, Staveford, Gulhaven); Wilwick; Sceaux (ball location); Père-Lachaise cemetery; Rue Mouffetard; Rue De la Barrière-des-Gobelins; harbor town of Dunstead. **Environmental progression**: Spring—frost silvering hedges, light early, smoke flat; Summer—warm air, sparrows chirping, bees humming in lavender, gulls quarrying, salt and tar scent from water, wind off water carries salt and tar, chimneys smoking flat, evening light early; **Autumn/Winter transition**: icy breeze through windows, snow falling, Candlemas sun promising snow that arrives, outer mist penetrating like whitish wadding, bell for vespers ringing thinly.

## Primary Locations
**LUXEMBOURG GARDENS**: Fountain basin with swans; statues including Leonidas, Spartacus, Gladiator; "his alley" on Rue de l'Ouest side with recurring bench; bench by Gladiator near other end. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus convent. **M. GILLENORMAND'S RESIDENCES**: Rue Férou; Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. **GORBEAU HOVEL**: 50-52, Salpêtrière district; Marius's attic cabinet, 30 francs annually. **JONDRETTE DEN** (Summer Year 4): Within or near Gorbeau house; abject, dirty, fetid, sordid; furniture: straw chair, infirm table, crockery, two pallets; dormer window four panes draped in spiders' webs; leprous walls with seams and scars; obscene sketches in charcoal; repulsive moisture; let for forty francs yearly; floor uneven, antique plaster blackened; fireplace with brazier, pot, broken boards, suspended rags, bird-cage, ashes. Attic large with projections, angles, black holes, bays, promontories; horrible unfathomable nooks. One pallet near door, one near window. Colored engraving "THE DREAM" (black frame): sleeping woman and child, eagle in cloud with crown, woman thrusting crown away, Napoleon in glory on blue column with yellow capital. Wooden panel stood on ground against wall, picture-face turned to wall. Windows with broken panes. One bed occupied by Jondrette woman. Dark interior (newcomers experience cellar-like darkness; inhabitants accustomed to twilight). **M. MABEUF'S COTTAGE**: Village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; thatched cottage; fifty crowns yearly; three rooms, enclosed garden.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette
Valjean integrated as assistant gardener in convent; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete. Cosette became convent scholar; believes Valjean is her father; adores him. Fauchelevent sole ally aware of full presence. Nuns unaware of circumstances.

## Javert's Pursuit
Attached to Paris police after Valjean's escape. **Status (Winter Year 3)**: Established sentinels, organized traps around Gorbeau house; confident convict nearby.

## Marius Pontmercy: Development, Passion, and Crisis

**Identity and age**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old (Spring Year 4); three years since left grandfather. **Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction regarding baron title and Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Lost medallion of black shagreen; believes grandfather burned it.

**Political evolution (Winter Year 3 → Spring Year 4)**: Converted to Bonapartism and republicanism; political fevers dissipated through reverie; Revolution of 1830 calmed views. Sympathies to humanity over nation, woman over people, idea over deed, poet over hero. Preferred introspection to action.

**Material condition (Spring Year 4)**: Gorbeau cabinet 30 francs annually; daily sustenance 20 sous (365 francs yearly); clothing 100 francs; linen/washing 100 francs. Total: 450 francs. Earned approximately seven hundred francs yearly. **Refused advancement (Winter Year 3)**: M. Magimel offered fifteen hundred francs yearly—Marius refused to preserve liberty and dignity. Deliberately stopped working to dedicate time to thought and meditation.

**Grandfather quarrel**: Violent estrangement three years ago without rapprochement—"Marius was the brass vase, while Father Gillenormand was the iron pot." Grandfather's suffering locked within breast.

**Relationship with Friends of the A B C**: Met Courfeyrac at Place Saint-Michel; became good friends. Did not enter decidedly into group but remained cordial. Close to **M. Mabeuf**—owed him revolution within soul; indebted for knowing and loving his father. **Recent social activities (Spring Year 4)**: Dined with Courfeyrac; breakfasted at Café Voltaire.

## The Mysterious Couple, Girl (Cosette), and Marius's Passion

**Initial six-month observation (over one year prior)**: Marius noticed man approximately sixty (M. Leblanc) and very young girl (thirteen/fourteen) on Luxembourg bench daily. Man: retired military officer, robust, weary, kindly; wore blue trousers and coat, broad-brimmed hat, black cravat, white shirt, white hair. Girl: thin, awkward, promise of handsome eyes; wore convent scholar dress.

**Six-month interruption**: Observation ceased for unknown reason.

**Reunion and girl's transformation (Summer Year 3)**: Girl became well-dressed young maiden. Wore black damask dress and cape, white crape bonnet, white gloves, carved Chinese ivory parasol handle, silken shoe.

**Marius's indifference (Summer Year 3)**: When she raised eyelids, Marius found only child's glance. She looked indifferently. Marius paid no further attention.

**First meaningful glance and awakening (Spring Year 4)**: On warm day in Luxembourg, their glances met. Marius perceived he wore everyday clothes; resolved to dress differently. Following day wore new coat, seated himself surveying her. Left only when gates closed. His worship of his father retreated to depths of soul.

**Marius's emotional transformation**: Love came. Brain felt on fire. She appeared beautiful, wholly feminine and angelic. Vexed about dust on boots. Followed her with eyes until disappeared. Walked like madman; ate and spoke excitedly; laughed uproariously.

**Strategic approach (Spring Year 4)**: Combined stations behind trees and pedestals with diplomacy to be seen by girl and unseen by M. Leblanc. Sometimes remained motionless half-hour in shade. She bent upon Marius all reveries of virginal and passionate eye.

**M. Leblanc's response**: Noticed something. Often rose when Marius arrived and moved to bench by Gladiator near other end. Marius did not pursue. M. Leblanc made daughter pass carriage entrance first, then stared intently at Marius.

**Escalation and handkerchief (Spring Year 4)**: Found handkerchief on bench after they left. Very simple, white, fine, exhaled ineffable perfume. Marked with letters U. F. Marius immediately thought "Ursule!" Kissed handkerchief, placed on heart during day; laid beneath lips at night.

**Leg incident and jealousy (Spring Year 4)**: Brisk May breeze lifted dress to height of garter. **A leg of exquisite shape appeared. Marius saw it. He was exasperated and furious.** Girl hastily thrust down dress with divinely troubled motion. Marius determined to be vexed. **Harsh and capricious jealousy of the flesh awakened in his heart.** When she passed bench, Marius darted sullen and ferocious glance. She gave slight straightening up with backward movement: "Well, what is the matter?"

**Veteran encounter and paroxysm**: A bent, wrinkled, pale veteran in Louis XV uniform bearing soldier's cross of Saint-Louis crossed walk. Marius thought he perceived man had extremely well satisfied air; struck him aged cynic addressed him fraternal and merry wink. **Marius reached paroxysm of jealousy.** "Perhaps he was there! Perhaps he saw!" Felt desire to exterminate the veteran.

**M. Leblanc and girl's disappearance (Summer-Autumn Year 4)**: Summer passed, autumn came, winter arrived. Neither set foot in Luxembourg garden again. **Marius had but one thought—to gaze once more on that sweet and adorable face.** Fell into black melancholy. All was over. Work disgusted him; walking tired him. Everything had disappeared.

**Self-reproach (Autumn Year 4)**: Heaped hundred reproaches on himself: "Why did I follow her? I was happy at mere sight! Why wish to have more?" Confided nothing to Courfeyrac, but Courfeyrac guessed everything.

**Ball at Sceaux (September Year 4)**: Allowed himself taken to ball hoping to find her. Did not see her. Left friends and returned home on foot alone through night, weary, feverish, with sad and troubled eyes.

**Miraculous rediscovery (Summer Year 4, Jondrette den)**: **Marius perceived the girl (Cosette) in Jondrette hovel when she arrived with M. Leblanc to distribute charity.** "It was certainly she. Marius could hardly distinguish her through the luminous vapor which had suddenly spread before his eyes. It was that sweet, absent being, that star which had beamed upon him for six months." **Marius shuddered in dismay, felt on brink of bursting into tears.** His heart palpitated; seemed to him he had lost his soul and just found it again. During entire visit, Marius lived in ecstasy; eyes remained fixed on girl; heart seized and wholly enveloped her from her very first step. He contemplated not the girl but "that light which wore a satin pelisse and a velvet bonnet." Did not know sound of her voice. All exclamations and trumpet bursts of Jondrette drowned her words. **He devoured her with his eyes. Could not believe divine creature was in midst of vile creatures in that monstrous lair. Seemed to him he beheld humming-bird in midst of toads.**

**Attempt to follow (Summer Year 4, post-Jondrette den)**: When she took departure, Marius had one thought—to follow her, cling to her trace, learn where she lived. Leaped down from commode, seized hat. Rushed in their direction, caught sight of fiacre descending Rue Mouffetard, already far off. Could not overtake; would be noticed. **Perceived empty cab passing boulevard. To jump into cab and follow fiacre was sure, efficacious, and free from danger. BUT—lack of twenty-four sous prevented him. Marius stared at retreating cabriolet with bewildered air.** "For the lack of four and twenty sous, he was losing his joy, his happiness, his love!" Reflected bitterly on five francs given that morning to elder Jondrette daughter. **"If he had had those five francs, he would have been saved, he would have been born again, he would have emerged from the limbo and darkness... he might have re-knotted the black thread of his destiny to that beautiful golden thread."** Returned to hovel in despair.

## The Jondrette Family, Ambush Plot, and Present Crisis

**First girl's appearance and condition (Spring Year 4, morning)**: About seven o'clock, very young girl stood in half-open door. **She was frail, emaciated, slender creature**: nothing but chemise and petticoat on chilled, shivering nakedness. **Form of young girl who missed her youth; look of corrupt old woman; fifty years mingled with fifteen.** One of those beings both feeble and horrible.

**Second girl (eldest daughter) and letter delivery (Summer Year 4)**: Found M. Leblanc at church. Handed him letter. He read it, asked "Where do you live, my child?" She answered she would show him. He said no, requested address. She gave address: last door in corridor, on right. He seemed surprised, hesitated, then said: "Never mind, I will come." After mass, watched him leave church with daughter; saw them enter carriage.

**Jondrette's recognition and wife's rage (Summer Year 4, just now)**: Jondrette returned breathlessly from outside. Daughters seated near fireplace, elder dressing younger's wounded hand. Wife sunk back on bed with astonishment. Jondrette paced with long strides, eyes extraordinary. **Whispered name in wife's ear sufficed to rouse this somnolent woman; from repulsive she became terrible.** Wife cried in rage: "It is not possible! My daughters going barefoot, no gowns! What! A satin pelisse, a velvet bonnet, boots—more than two hundred francs' worth of clothes! So one would think she was a lady! The other was hideous, this one is not so bad-looking! It can't be she!"

**Jondrette's scheme and timing (Summer Year 4, evening imminent)**: Jondrette announced: "The Crœsus is caught, or as good as caught! Everything is arranged. I have seen some people. He will come here this evening at six o'clock. To bring sixty francs, the rascal! Did you notice how I played that game on him, my sixty francs, my landlord, my fourth of February? So he will come at six o'clock! That's the hour when our neighbor goes to his dinner. Mother Bougon is off washing dishes in the city. There's not a soul in the house. The neighbor never comes home until eleven o'clock. The children shall stand on watch. You shall help us. He will give in."

**Wife's outburst (demand for subsistence)**: "Thunder! I was a parishioner of the parish of die-of-hunger-if-you-have-a-fire,-die-of-cold-if-you-have-bread! I have had enough of misery! I am not joking any longer! I want to eat till I am full, I want to drink my fill! to gormandize! to sleep! to do nothing! I want to have my turn, so I do, come now! before I die! I want to be a bit of a millionnaire!"

## Marius's Recognition and Dilemma (Summer Year 4, 1 P.M.)

**Recognition of danger**: Marius overheard conversation. Not one enigma hoped solved had been elucidated; all rendered more dense. Knew nothing more about beautiful maiden and M. Leblanc except Jondrette acquainted with them. **Through mysterious words, caught glimpse: ambush in course of preparation, dark but terrible trap; both incurring great danger, she probably, her father certainly. Must be saved; hideous plots of Jondrettes must be thwarted; web of spiders broken.**

**Nature of Marius's character**: **Dreamer as he was, firm and energetic by nature. Habits of solitary meditation developed sympathy and compassion, perhaps diminished irritation, but left intact power of waxing indignant; had kindliness of brahmin and severity of judge; took pity upon toad, but crushed viper. Now glance directed into hole of vipers; nest of monsters beneath his eyes.**

**Joy amid horror**: **He experienced sort of joy at idea that it might be granted to him perhaps to render service to one whom he loved.**

**Critical obstacle (present, 1 P.M., five hours before trap springs)**: Did not know their address. They reappeared instant, plunged back into immense depths of Paris. Should he wait for M. Leblanc at door evening at six, warn him? But Jondrette and men would see him on watch; spot lonely; they stronger; would devise means to seize or get him away. **One o'clock had just struck, trap to be sprung at six. Marius had five hours before him.**

**Providence and five francs**: On way, **rendered justice to Providence. Reflected that had he not given five francs to Jondrette girl that morning, he would have followed M. Leblanc's fiacre, remained ignorant of everything, no obstacle to Jondrette trap, M. Leblanc and daughter would be lost, no doubt.**

## Friends of the A B C, Patron-Minette, and Criminal Underground

**Friends of the A B C**: Declared themselves Friends of the A B C—_Abaissé_, the debased (the people). Secret society in embryonic state. Meetings back room Café Musain. Members: Enjolras, Combeferre, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Courfeyrac, Bahorel, Lesgle/Laigle de Meaux, Joly, Grantaire. Most students; cordial with working classes.

**Philosophical discourse on social substructure**: All human societies have subterranean dimensions. Beneath social construction: religious, philosophical, economic, revolutionary mines. **The third lower floor (_le troisième dessous_)**: Below all mines, lies deepest stratum—**grave of shadows, cellar of blind, _Inferi_.** Wild spectres roam here, almost beasts, almost phantoms, unconcerned with universal progress. Two step-mothers: ignorance and misery. Guide: necessity. Satisfaction: appetite. Brutally voracious—ferocious as tiger. From suffering pass to crime. Man becomes dragon. Vault formed of ignorance. **All others above have one object—suppress it.** So long as society remains what it is, they remain what they are.

**Patron-Minette: Criminal association**: Members Babet, Gueulemer, Claquesous, Montparnasse. **Gueulemer**: Six feet high, Hercules of no defined position. Lair: sewer of Arche-Marion. Assassin through coolness. **Claquesous**: He was night. Emerged from hole at nightfall, returned before daylight. Hole location unknown. Addressed accomplices only in absolute darkness, back turned. If candle brought, put on mask. Ventriloquist. Never seen without mask. **Function**: Four ruffians formed Proteus, furnish canvas for ambushes in Seine department.

## English Provincial Towns: Movements, Incidents, Rumors, and Claims

**Population movements**: Rozek Stenenridge rode out of Dungate; living in Wilwick by next market day. Yera Haskick (Dunstead → Kelmere); Rinelle (Kelford → Torton); Kadrek Brackick (followed to Torton). Luena Stenenridge followed him to Wilwick within month. **Deaths**: Luwyn Brackick died of kick from cart horse; laid in churchyard at Dunstead. **Births**: Ferald and Isvie Stenworth (Dunstead, parents Luwyn Brackick); Zavus Prydenridge (Ostcombe, parents Wenelle and Rovus); Bremira Corrford (daughter of Kassa Brackick and Ulrald Corrford, Dunstead).

**Claims and rumors**: Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged (**confirmed by Lurald telling Ulrald Corrford**). Wenelle Lindmere drowned crossing estuary (rumor, no body). **Granary fire set on purpose (rumor—confirmed: Luena Stenenridge confided to Rozek that Dunstead granary fire was set on purpose; later Rozek confided to Pewyn Stenenridge that fire at Dunstead granary was set on purpose)**. Kadan Corrley burned letter from Yera Haskick revealing mill ledger rewritten. Kassa Brackick confided mill ledger rewritten. Fenelle Lindmere confided Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family (**later Fenelle told Peten Haskick this**). Price of salt scandal discussed.

**Current incidents (Spring-Summer Year 4)**: Lura Haskick laughed at story nobody else found funny. Ferald Stenworth complained of aching back. Dog barked at nothing then went quiet. Ferald hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step. Argued with carter over oats price. Lura told Fenelle "You look tired"; Fenelle did not deny it. Luena watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly. Bremira fell asleep before fire. Thizek read almanac aloud. Conversations about weather, harvest, lame horse. Nerine, Rovus, Isric, Gadrek, Havie, Yedan, Vesmira engaged in similar mundane activities. Isric gave up being smith, took work as glazier. **Luena bought ribbon at stall and then regretted it.** **Rozek hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing the step. Marald Corrford argued with carter over price of oats. Marald walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Lura and Lurald Stenworth talked of nothing much—weather, harvest, lame horse. Kassa told Marald Corrford "You look tired"; Marald did not deny it. Marald Corrford gave amber map to Ulrald Corrford. Youngest son of Yedan Corrford gave amber map to Ulrald Corrford.** **Rozek Stenenridge won copper chalice from Luena at cards, fairly, and kept it.**
